A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Interact2Ar study and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Existing content can be reliably matched across pagination and citation renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Inter-X experiments, evaluator robustness tests, memory ablations, and a user study with 35 participants.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds text-encoder experiments, interaction-quality measurements, and qualitative contact comparisons.

M1.justification: The proposed architecture, losses, autoregressive procedure, and Mixed Memory mechanism remain unchanged. Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B is tested as an ablation alternative; it does not replace CLIP in the default model.

E1.justification: Both versions use Inter-X for full-body interaction generation and retain the same adaptive interaction tasks. The added metrics and hand-contact examples examine existing coverage without introducing another dataset, population, or distinct test scenario.

E2.justification: New Table C evaluates Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B against CLIP as a text-encoding alternative. The motion-generation comparators remain T2M, InterGen, and InterMask; newly cited dance methods supply metrics rather than additional evaluated generators.

E3.justification: Appendix B.4 adds contact frequency, pairwise-distance FID, interaction penetration volume, and physical foot contact measurements. This substantially extends evaluation to direct contact and physical plausibility beyond the existing feature-based and jerk metrics. Table C also introduces a text-encoder comparison; existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 adds a focused CLIP-versus-Qwen encoder ablation. Section C and Figure B add grab and handshake contact case studies, while B.4 identifies foot-sliding errors. Existing memory ablations and evaluator robustness tests are retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and A retain the same statements specifying 20 evaluations and 95% confidence intervals. New Tables C and D use the existing plus/minus reporting format without introducing a different run count, seed policy, or statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Existing Tables 1–3, A, and B are numerically unchanged, but new results substantially expand evidence about encoder choice and physical interaction quality. Table C reports CLIP versus Qwen FID of 0.277 versus 0.389. Table D reports Interact2Ar versus InterMask distance-based FID of 2.406 versus 5.593 and foot-contact scores of 0.268 versus 0.339. These are added evaluations, not improvements over v1's scores.

T1.justification: Equations 1–14 retain the same losses, motion decomposition, and memory definitions. The added metrics are adopted and described without new mathematical results, assumptions, proofs, or substantive derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims concerning full-body autoregressive interaction generation, Mixed Memory, improved evaluators, and adaptive applications. The appendix additions supply supporting evidence without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 tentatively attributes limited encoder differences to low textual diversity. B.4 newly acknowledges foot sliding across evaluated methods and suggests additional data or post-processing as possible remedies. The existing body-shape and hand-contact limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4 newly clarifies that metrics are calculated per interaction rather than per individual, and B.3 identifies the tested Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B variant. These are limited documentation additions; existing implementation settings and the promise to release code and checkpoints upon acceptance are unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for Qwen3-VL embeddings, CLIP, InterDance, Duolando, and EDGE to support the new experiments and metrics. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 expands the supplementary overview, adds Sections B.3–B.4, renames B.2 to Extended Memory Ablation, revises the qualitative discussion and acknowledgments, and fixes Interact2Ar spelling errors. The main narrative and overall section organization remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables C and D and Figure B's close-up contact comparisons. Existing figures and table structures are retained, with localized text reflow and a corrected Figure 5 caption rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, the direct contact, penetration, and foot-contact measurements strengthen validation of interaction realism, while the encoder ablation and explicit foot-sliding limitation improve scrutiny. The gains are bounded: new experimental procedures remain sparsely documented, and B.3's description of encoder differences as minimal is insufficiently reconciled with Table C's retrieval and FID differences.
